# Test that a panic in a benchmark fails the run. The benchmark goroutine
# used to signal that it was done while the panic unwound, so the run could
# print PASS and exit 0 before the panic ended the process. Each panic value
# below has a slow Error method, which the runtime calls before it exits,
# so without the fix every run here would pass.

# A panic in the first iteration, which run1 executes.
! go test -run '^$' -bench '^BenchmarkPanic$' -benchtime=1x benchpanic
! stdout ^ok
! stdout ^PASS
stdout 'panic: boom'
stdout FAIL.*benchpanic

# A panic in a later iteration, which launch executes.
! go test -run '^$' -bench '^BenchmarkPanicLater$' -benchtime=2x benchpanic
! stdout ^ok
! stdout ^PASS
stdout 'panic: later'
stdout FAIL.*benchpanic

# A panic in a sub-benchmark.
! go test -run '^$' -bench '^BenchmarkPanicSub$' -benchtime=1x benchpanic
! stdout ^ok
! stdout ^PASS
stdout 'panic: sub'
stdout FAIL.*benchpanic

# A direct runtime.Goexit, which neither returns nor stops with FailNow or
# SkipNow, fails as it does in a test.
! go test -run '^$' -bench '^BenchmarkGoexit$' -benchtime=1x benchpanic
! stdout ^ok
stdout 'panic: test executed panic\(nil\) or runtime.Goexit'
stdout FAIL.*benchpanic

-- go.mod --
module benchpanic

go 1.16
-- x_test.go --
package benchpanic

import (
	"runtime"
	"testing"
	"time"
)

// slowErr delays the runtime's report of a panic, giving the goroutine
// waiting on the benchmark time to finish the run first.
type slowErr string

func (e slowErr) Error() string {
	time.Sleep(time.Second)
	return string(e)
}

func BenchmarkPanic(b *testing.B) {
	panic(slowErr("boom"))
}

func BenchmarkPanicLater(b *testing.B) {
	if b.N > 1 {
		panic(slowErr("later"))
	}
}

func BenchmarkPanicSub(b *testing.B) {
	b.Run("sub", func(b *testing.B) {
		panic(slowErr("sub"))
	})
}

func BenchmarkGoexit(b *testing.B) {
	runtime.Goexit()
}
